question: can the model run on bf16 master weights so that the 1432 Cast kernels (22.4% of the step) disappear, keeping fp32 only inside the optimizer?

probe.setup: real model weight shapes (192x192 proj, 768x192 gate, 192x132 band linear), Xavier-ish init, per-tensor grad rms 0.5 (matches the run's grad_norm ~0.5 over ~600 tensors), AdamW lr 5e-4 / wd 0.01 / betas 0.9,0.999 / eps 1e-8, 1000 steps, fp32 reference
probe.verdict: rounding loss exceeds 1% - use the Kahan variant

why_the_estimate_was_wrong: the a-priori estimate compared lr (5e-4) with half an ulp of |w|~0.03 (~1.2e-4) and concluded updates survive by 4x. But AdamW's per-element step is lr * m/(sqrt(v)+eps), not lr: for gradient noise the ratio m/sqrt(v) is ~0.1-0.3 for most elements, and smaller still for the many near-zero weights, so the effective |dw| sits under the ulp and 60-75% of the elements never move at all. After 1000 steps the bf16 model has drifted 12% (rel_rms) away from the fp32 trajectory.

decision.kahan_variant: numerically acceptable (2.2-2.4e-03 weight drift, i.e. under the 9.2e-03 the current autocast bf16 already shows) BUT it needs a persistent fp32 shadow + compensation tensor per parameter, so it re-introduces one fp32->bf16 cast per parameter per step. The 1432 Cast kernels are per *layer* per op, ~600 params would give ~600 casts, i.e. the saving shrinks and the code becomes a hand-written fp32-master optimizer - not the 'cast once in the optimizer' this task was premised on.
decision.consequence: the bulk of this task's expected win does not exist in the simple form, so per the stated stop rule the remaining two items are re-scoped, not forced through: (2) Triton RMSNorm and (3) band_split default stay valid but their measured ceilings are ~20 ms and ~6-8 ms respectively (FUSION task), i.e. they cannot close the 1088 ms -> 850 ms gap either

fixed-dtype bf16 for the *inference* path only (measured 11.616 -> 10.634 ms there)
attack the backward of LocalBandBlock directly with make_fx + pass merging, which is the only lever with a >100 ms budget
